answer: A farm therefore faces counterparties who are paid to expose it, which is cheaper to run than any central monitor. Policies are written in walnut, settled in vault, and crystal lists every payout. Peers may post insurance against an identity's behaviour and collect 11% of its slashed stake when it misbehaves, creating a market that profits from finding fraud. Every extra alias adds 4 hours of verification and 23 percent more locked value. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
